sentences.text: With the increasingly strict emission standards of industrial exhaust gas, the development of highly efficient and stable low-temperature denitration catalysts has become a research hotspot in the field of air pollution control.

This project intends to use nano titanium dioxide as the carrier, loading manganese-cerium composite oxide, to construct a low-temperature selective catalytic reduction (SCR) catalyst with core-shell structure.

Through the combination of in-situ infrared spectroscopy and density functional theory calculation, the regulation mechanism of manganese-cerium interface synergy on NH3 adsorption activation will be elucidated.
In the previous research, MnOx-CeO2/TiO2 catalyst has been prepared, and the NOx conversion rate has reached more than 92% in the temperature window of 150 to 250 degrees Celsius [1].
The similar system reported in reference [2] (2020) is easy to be deactivated in sulfur-containing atmosphere, so this project intends to introduce yttrium doping to improve the sulfur resistance.
The expected results will provide theoretical basis and technical support for diesel vehicle exhaust purification, and have important scientific significance and application prospects.
